data.name: Geronimo
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin name Geronimus, which means 'ready for war'. In Christian tradition, Geronimo is the name of a legendary Native American warrior and saint.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes courage and determination in the face of adversity.

in_hebrew.name: ג'ירונימו
in_hebrew.meaning: השם ג'ירונימו לא נמצא במקרא, משמעותו לא ברורה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ג'ירונימו אינו מופיע במקרא העברי. מקורו של השם אינו ברור, אך יש המשערים כי הוא קשור לשם היווני הירונימוס (Hieronymus), שפירושו 'שם קדוש'. אין אזכור לשם זה בספרות היהדות או בנצרות העברית.

in_greek.name: Γερόνυμο
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Γερόνυμο δεν έχει άμεση βιβλική σημασία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Γερόνυμο δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα στις σελίδες της Καινής Διαθήκης. Παράγωγο από το ελληνικό 'γέροντας' που σημαίνει 'γηραιός' και 'ὄνυμα' που σημαίνει 'όνομα', θα μπορούσε να ερμηνευτεί ως 'ευγενές όνομα' ή 'όνομα του γέροντος'. Στην ιστορία της Εκκλησίας, δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα αυτό.

in_latin.name: Geronimo
in_latin.meaning: Nomen Geronimo significationem profundam non habet
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Geronimo a linguis externis derivatum videtur. Etymologia remota a voce Graeca 'γέροντας' (senex) et ὄνυμα (nomen) conjungitur. In ecclesia primitiva, non apparet nomen Geronimo directe. Usus modernus indicat derivationem de Hieronymus (sanctus), qui fuit scriptor sanctus et theologus christianus.

in_english.name: Geronimo
in_english.meaning: The name Geronimo signifies sacred name or venerable
in_english.long_meaning: The name Geronimo does not directly appear in the Bible. It is derived from the Greek name 'Hieronymus', meaning 'sacred name' or 'venerable name'. This name was popularized by Saint Jerome, a 4th-century Christian priest, biblical scholar, and theologian. Geronimo is often associated with bravery and courage due to its connection with the famous Apache leader Geronimo. In Christian tradition, the name represents spiritual strength and devotion.

biblical_reference.note: The name does not appear in the Bible.

saint_reference.note: The name is associated with Saint Jerome, a Doctor of the Church.

data.cultural_impact: The name Geronimo has a significant cultural impact, as it is synonymous with bravery, strength, and defiance. It is best known as the name of a famous Native American warrior, Geronimo (Him-dall-na-jay) of the Bedonkohe band of the Chiricahua Apache tribe. Born in 1829, he gained fame for his resistance to Mexican and American encroachment on Apache lands. Geronimo's name became a symbol of Native American resistance, calling to mind the spirit of defiance and unyielding determination that is often associated with the Native American experience.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Geronimo is believed to have embraced Christianity late in life. According to legend, while imprisoned at Fort Sill, Oklahoma, in 1886, Geronimo had a vision in which Jesus appeared to him and offered him salvation. Geronimo is said to have accepted Jesus' offer, asking for forgiveness for his past actions and dedicating the remainder of his life to Christian praxis. As a result, Geronimo is remembered not just as a one-dimensional figure of resistance, but as a complex individual who, in his later years, sought redemption and spiritual growth. In this way, Geronimo's name takes on a spiritual significance, representing the transformative power of faith and the possibility of redeeming even the most difficult past.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Geronimo (c. 1460–1800) was a prominent Apache leader. The name Geronimo carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Geronimo signifies bravery and strength in the face of adversity. Named after the legendary Apache warrior, this name encourages resilience and determination against all odds. Embracing the spirit of Geronimo, one remains unyielding in the pursuit of freedom and justice.
